tts_summary:
Here's your post-close recap for Tuesday, September 22nd, 2026. Three names reported after the bell tonight — KB Home, Labcorp, and Worthington Enterprises — and the tone across the board was mixed with a cautious tilt on macro.

Let's start with KB Home. KBH posted a solid FQ3 earnings beat — one dollar and five cents versus the Street's eighty-nine cents. The upside was driven mostly by cost discipline, with the SG&A ratio beating expectations by about 0.30%, plus a little help from slightly better gross margins and deliveries. So far so good. But the FQ4 guide is where it gets messy. Gross margins and SG&A are both expected to come in a bit worse than the Street was modeling, even though delivery volumes are roughly inline. And management's macro commentary was blunt — they said the housing market is challenging and has gotten worse since their June report. Higher mortgage rates are crushing affordability, and geopolitical uncertainty is keeping prospective buyers on the sidelines. That's not a green light for the homebuilder sector. Treat this one as mixed at best.

Next up, Labcorp. LH got hit during the session, falling about 3%, and the culprit is CMS Medicare payment rate cuts. Management isn't happy about it — they said the new rates would impose steep annual payment cuts that threaten patient access to lab services. To their credit, they're reaffirming the long-term guidance they laid out at the September 10th analyst meeting, covering 2026 through 2029. But here's the catch — the specific 2027 impact won't be quantified until Q4 earnings in February. That's a long time to sit with uncertainty, and the stock's reaction today tells you the market doesn't love the setup. Bearish read near-term.

Finally, Worthington Enterprises. WOR was the cleanest print of the night. FQ1 EPS came in at eighty-two cents versus the Street's seventy-five, EBITDA hit seventy-four million versus sixty-nine and a half expected, and revenue grew thirteen percent year-over-year to three forty-four million, ahead of the three thirty-two estimate. But the real headline is the data center angle — management specifically called out rapidly growing demand for their engineered ASME tanks used in liquid cooling systems for data centers. That's a high-conviction growth driver in a space the market is actively rewarding. Bullish read on WOR.

Bottom line tonight: housing remains under pressure, lab services face a regulatory overhang, and industrial names with data center exposure continue to find tailwinds. Stay selective, and watch for any broader read-through from KBH's commentary into the homebuilder space tomorrow.
